ES.visaType: Type D Long-Stay Study Visa (Visado Nacional de Larga Duración)
ES.duration: Required for stays >90 days (full semester). Short-stay Schengen visa for visits <90 days.
requiredDocuments: Valid passport (min. 1 year validity beyond intended stay)
Completed national visa application form
2 recent passport photographs (35×45mm, white background)
University admission letter (Carta de Admisión from URJC)
Proof of sufficient funds (Erasmus grant letter + bank statements)
Health insurance valid in Spain (min. €30,000 coverage)
Proof of accommodation in Spain (rental contract or residence letter)
Criminal background check (apostilled in your country)
Medical certificate
Visa fee payment receipt (~€80)
ES.notes: Apply at the Spanish embassy/consulate in your home country at least 8 weeks before travel. Appointments must be in person. After arriving in Spain, apply for the TIE (Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero) at the Oficina de Extranjería within 30 days of arrival.

GB.visaType: Student Visa (UK Visas and Immigration — Student route)
GB.duration: Course length + additional time. For ~5 month semester, Standard Visitor may apply.
requiredDocuments: Valid passport
Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from Bangor University
Online UK visa application at gov.uk
Biometric enrolment at UK Visa Application Centre in your country
Bank statements showing funds for full stay
Proof of English language proficiency (IELTS Academic 5.5+ or equivalent)
Tuberculosis (TB) test results (if from a listed country — check gov.uk)
Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) payment — £776/year (grants NHS access)
Visa fee: £490
GB.notes: Apply for your UK Student Visa at least 6–8 weeks before the course start date. If your semester is under 6 months, confirm with Bangor University whether a Standard Visitor Visa (£115, no CAS needed) is sufficient. Your BRP (Biometric Residence Permit) will be issued in the UK — collect it from the designated Post Office within 10 days of arrival.

MX.visaType: Visa de Visitante (Visitor Visa — no work permit)
MX.duration: Up to 180 days — sufficient for the 3-week summer school
requiredDocuments: Valid passport (6+ months validity beyond travel dates)
Completed Mexican visa application form
Recent passport photograph
Proof of enrollment/invitation letter from UATx
Bank statements proving sufficient funds (~USD 1,500 minimum)
Visa fee (~USD 36)
MX.notes: Apply at the Mexican embassy or consulate serving your home country. Processing is usually 2–4 weeks. The summer school (6–8 weeks) is well within the 180-day visa validity. Upon arrival you receive an FMM card — keep it safe and return it when you leave Mexico.

PT.visaType: EU Student Mobility Notification — AIMA Art. 91 (No visa required if holding a Spanish residence permit)
PT.duration: Up to 360 days (AIMA Declaration issued electronically)
PT.processingTime: Variable — AIMA issues Declaration once no objections are raised
requiredDocuments: Form Template 6 (Modelo 6) — download at: https://aima.gov.pt/media/pages/documents/23b161701a-1772620073/modelo-6.pdf
Copy of valid passport
Copy of valid Spanish residence permit (issued by Spain as the EU Member State that granted the permit)
Criminal record from your country of nationality (or from any country where you resided for more than 1 year before Portugal) — must be duly certified and within its validity period
Proof of admission under a European Union or multilateral mobility programme — Letter of Acceptance or Statement from the Portuguese higher education institution
Proof of health insurance valid in Portugal
Proof of fee payment by bank transfer to IBAN PT50 0781 0112 0112 0014 4001 1 (as indicated on Form 6; send together with all documents)
PT.notes: Send all documents by email to comunicacao.mobilidade.ue@aima.gov.pt. In your email, indicate your expected date of entry into Portugal and expected date of departure, and state that your educational institution confirms compliance with all necessary requirements. AIMA will issue a Declaration authorising you to remain in Portugal for up to 360 days, sent electronically to the email address you provide. ⚠️ If you do NOT hold a Spanish residence permit, you must follow the standard procedures and obtain a Portuguese Student Visa (Type D) through the Portuguese diplomatic network before travelling. Contact AIMA directly at comunicacao.mobilidade.ue@aima.gov.pt for any queries.

GB.visaType: Student Visa (study >6 months) or Standard Visitor Visa (study ≤6 months)
GB.duration: Semester 2 is ~5 months — confirm exact length with Bangor University
requiredDocuments: Valid passport
Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from Bangor University
Online UK visa application at gov.uk
Biometric enrolment at UK Visa Application Centre
Bank statements showing sufficient funds
Proof of English language proficiency (IELTS/TOEFL or exemption)
Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) payment — £776/year

MX.visaType: No Visa Required — Tourist entry up to 180 days (FMM card on arrival)

MX.notes: Your nationality enters Mexico visa-free for up to 180 days. Keep your FMM card safe — return it on departure.

GB.visaType: UK Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA)
GB.duration: Up to 6 months per visit
GB.processingTime: Usually within 1 day (up to 3 working days)
requiredDocuments: Valid passport
Digital photo of your face
Email address
Credit or debit card (£16 fee, rising to £20 from April 2026)
GB.notes: Apply via the UK ETA app or at gov.uk/eta. Links to your passport; valid for 2 years or until your passport expires (whichever is sooner). Permits multiple trips of up to 6 months each. An ETA does not guarantee entry to the UK. For studies exceeding 6 months, a UK Student Visa is required instead.

MX.visaType: Visa-Free Entry
requiredDocuments: Valid ordinary passport
Immigration card (completed on arrival for air entry)
Forma Migratoria Múltiple — FMM (required for land border entry; obtain free online at inm.gob.mx before travel)

For short-term study (≤180 days): acceptance letter from a Mexican institution in the National Educational System, stating your full name, level and area of study, course name, start and end dates, fee cost, and institution contact

For short-term study: proof of economic solvency — bank statements showing an average monthly balance of approx. $2,053 CAD (or equivalent) over the past 3 months, or a scholarship/employment/pension letter
MX.notes: Citizens of visa-exempt countries may enter Mexico without a visa for tourism, transit, or short-term study for up to 180 days. For study purposes carry an acceptance letter from your Mexican educational institution and proof of financial solvency. Solvency may be shown by a parent or guardian if you are under 25, or by a scholarship letter from the institution. Cross land borders with a completed FMM form. Verify current requirements at the nearest Mexican consulate or embassy before travelling.

GB.processingTime: Usually within 1 day (up to 3 working days)
requiredDocuments: Valid passport
Digital photo of your face
Email address
Credit or debit card (£16 fee, rising to £20 from April 2026)
GB.notes: Apply via the UK ETA app or at gov.uk/eta. Links to your passport; valid for 2 years or until your passport expires (whichever is sooner). Permits multiple trips of up to 6 months each. An ETA does not guarantee entry to the UK. For studies exceeding 6 months, a UK Student Visa is required instead.

MX.visaType: No Visa Required — Tourist entry up to 180 days (FMM card on arrival)
requiredDocuments: Valid passport
FMM card (completed on arrival)
Return/onward flight ticket
UATx invitation letter (recommended)
MX.notes: Your nationality enters Mexico visa-free for up to 180 days. Keep your FMM card safe — return it on departure.

PT.visaType: EU Student Mobility Notification — AIMA Art. 91 (No visa required if holding a Spanish residence permit)
PT.duration: Up to 360 days (AIMA Declaration issued electronically)
PT.processingTime: Variable — AIMA issues Declaration once no objections are raised
requiredDocuments: Form Template 6 (Modelo 6) — download at: https://aima.gov.pt/media/pages/documents/23b161701a-1772620073/modelo-6.pdf
Copy of valid passport
Copy of valid Spanish residence permit (issued by Spain as the EU Member State that granted the permit)
Criminal record from your country of nationality (or from any country where you resided for more than 1 year before Portugal) — must be duly certified and within its validity period
Proof of admission under a European Union or multilateral mobility programme — Letter of Acceptance or Statement from the Portuguese higher education institution
Proof of health insurance valid in Portugal
Proof of fee payment by bank transfer to IBAN PT50 0781 0112 0112 0014 4001 1 (as indicated on Form 6; send together with all documents)
PT.notes: Send all documents by email to comunicacao.mobilidade.ue@aima.gov.pt. In your email, indicate your expected date of entry into Portugal and expected date of departure, and state that your educational institution confirms compliance with all necessary requirements. AIMA will issue a Declaration authorising you to remain in Portugal for up to 360 days, sent electronically to the email address you provide. ⚠️ If you do NOT hold a Spanish residence permit, you must follow the standard procedures and obtain a Portuguese Student Visa (Type D) through the Portuguese diplomatic network before travelling. Contact AIMA directly at comunicacao.mobilidade.ue@aima.gov.pt for any queries.

ES.visaType: No Visa Required — EU/EEA Freedom of Movement
ES.duration: Unlimited right to reside; register at Registro Central de Extranjeros if staying >3 months
requiredDocuments: Valid EU/EEA passport or national identity card
University enrollment certificate (Carta de Admisión from URJC)
Registration at Registro Central de Extranjeros if staying >3 months (free, at police station)
ES.notes: As an EU/EEA citizen, you do not need a visa to study in Spain. If staying more than 3 months, register at the nearest Oficina de Extranjería or Comisaría de Policía with your passport and enrollment certificate. You will receive a certificate of registration (not a residence card). EHIC/CEAM card covers public healthcare.

MX.visaType: Visa-Free Entry
requiredDocuments: Valid ordinary passport
Immigration card (completed on arrival for air entry)
Forma Migratoria Múltiple — FMM (required for land border entry; obtain free online at inm.gob.mx before travel)

For short-term study (≤180 days): acceptance letter from a Mexican institution in the National Educational System, stating your full name, level and area of study, course name, start and end dates, fee cost, and institution contact

For short-term study: proof of economic solvency — bank statements showing an average monthly balance of approx. $2,053 CAD (or equivalent) over the past 3 months, or a scholarship/employment/pension letter
MX.notes: Citizens of visa-exempt countries may enter Mexico without a visa for tourism, transit, or short-term study for up to 180 days. For study purposes carry an acceptance letter from your Mexican educational institution and proof of financial solvency. Solvency may be shown by a parent or guardian if you are under 25, or by a scholarship letter from the institution. Cross land borders with a completed FMM form. Verify current requirements at the nearest Mexican consulate or embassy before travelling.

PT.visaType: No Visa Required — EU/EEA Freedom of Movement
PT.duration: Register at Câmara Municipal within 90 days if staying >3 months
PT.processingTime: N/A
requiredDocuments: Valid EU/EEA passport or national identity card
University enrollment certificate
Registration at local Câmara Municipal (within 90 days) — free
PT.notes: EU/EEA citizens do not need a visa or residence permit for Portugal. If staying more than 3 months, register at the Câmara Municipal (town hall) in your area — bring your passport and enrollment letter. You will also need a NIF (tax number) for renting and banking — get it at any Finanças office.

ES.visaType: Type D Long-Stay Study Visa (Visado Nacional de Larga Duración)
ES.duration: Required for stays >90 days (full semester). Short-stay Schengen visa for visits <90 days.
requiredDocuments: Valid passport (min. 1 year validity beyond intended stay)
Completed national visa application form
2 recent passport photographs (35×45mm, white background)
University admission letter (Carta de Admisión from URJC)
Proof of sufficient funds (Erasmus grant letter + bank statements)
Health insurance valid in Spain (min. €30,000 coverage)
Proof of accommodation in Spain (rental contract or residence letter)
Criminal background check (apostilled in your country)
Medical certificate
Visa fee payment receipt (~€80)
ES.notes: Apply at the Spanish embassy/consulate in your home country at least 8 weeks before travel. Appointments must be in person. After arriving in Spain, apply for the TIE (Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero) at the Oficina de Extranjería within 30 days of arrival.

GB.visaType: Student Visa (UK Visas and Immigration — Student route)
GB.duration: Course length + additional time. For ~5 month semester, Standard Visitor may apply.
requiredDocuments: Valid passport
Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from Bangor University
Online UK visa application at gov.uk
Biometric enrolment at UK Visa Application Centre in your country
Bank statements showing funds for full stay
Proof of English language proficiency (IELTS Academic 5.5+ or equivalent)
Tuberculosis (TB) test results (if from a listed country — check gov.uk)
Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) payment — £776/year (grants NHS access)
Visa fee: £490
GB.notes: Apply for your UK Student Visa at least 6–8 weeks before the course start date. If your semester is under 6 months, confirm with Bangor University whether a Standard Visitor Visa (£115, no CAS needed) is sufficient. Your BRP (Biometric Residence Permit) will be issued in the UK — collect it from the designated Post Office within 10 days of arrival.

MX.visaType: Visa de Visitante (Visitor Visa — no work permit)
MX.duration: Up to 180 days — sufficient for the 3-week summer school
requiredDocuments: Valid passport (6+ months validity beyond travel dates)
Completed Mexican visa application form
Recent passport photograph
Proof of enrollment/invitation letter from UATx
Bank statements proving sufficient funds (~USD 1,500 minimum)
Visa fee (~USD 36)
MX.notes: Apply at the Mexican embassy or consulate serving your home country. Processing is usually 2–4 weeks. The summer school (6–8 weeks) is well within the 180-day visa validity. Upon arrival you receive an FMM card — keep it safe and return it when you leave Mexico.

MX.visaType: Visa-Free Entry
requiredDocuments: Valid ordinary passport

Verify current requirements at the nearest Mexican consulate or embassy before travelling.

ES.visaType: No Visa Required — EU/EEA Freedom of Movement
ES.duration: Unlimited right to reside; register at Registro Central de Extranjeros if staying >3 months
requiredDocuments: Valid EU/EEA passport or national identity card
University enrollment certificate (Carta de Admisión from URJC)
Registration at Registro Central de Extranjeros if staying >3 months (free, at police station)
ES.notes: As an EU/EEA citizen, you do not need a visa to study in Spain. GB.visaType: UK Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA)
GB.duration: Up to 6 months per visit
GB.processingTime: Usually within 1 day (up to 3 working days)
requiredDocuments: Valid passport
Digital photo of your face
Email address
Credit or debit card (£16 fee, rising to £20 from April 2026)
GB.notes: Apply via the UK ETA app or at gov.uk/eta. Links to your passport; valid for 2 years or until your passport expires (whichever is sooner). Permits multiple trips of up to 6 months each. An ETA does not guarantee entry to the UK. For studies exceeding 6 months, a UK Student Visa is required instead.

MX.visaType: Visa-Free Entry
requiredDocuments: Valid ordinary passport
Immigration card (completed on arrival for air entry)
Forma Migratoria Múltiple — FMM (required for land border entry; obtain free online at inm.gob.mx before travel)

For short-term study (≤180 days): acceptance letter from a Mexican institution in the National Educational System, stating your full name, level and area of study, course name, start and end dates, fee cost, and institution contact

For short-term study: proof of economic solvency — bank statements showing an average monthly balance of approx. $2,053 CAD (or equivalent) over the past 3 months, or a scholarship/employment/pension letter
MX.notes: Citizens of visa-exempt countries may enter Mexico without a visa for tourism, transit, or short-term study for up to 180 days. For study purposes carry an acceptance letter from your Mexican educational institution and proof of financial solvency. Solvency may be shown by a parent or guardian if you are under 25, or by a scholarship letter from the institution. Cross land borders with a completed FMM form. Verify current requirements at the nearest Mexican consulate or embassy before travelling.

PT.visaType: No Visa Required — EU/EEA Freedom of Movement

PT.notes: EU/EEA citizens do not need a visa or residence permit for Portugal. If staying more than 3 months, register at the Câmara Municipal (town hall) in your area — bring your passport and enrollment letter. GB.visaType: UK Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA)
GB.duration: Up to 6 months per visit
GB.processingTime: Usually within 1 day (up to 3 working days)
requiredDocuments: Valid passport
Digital photo of your face
Email address
Credit or debit card (£16 fee, rising to £20 from April 2026)
GB.notes: Apply via the UK ETA app or at gov.uk/eta. Links to your passport; valid for 2 years or until your passport expires (whichever is sooner). Permits multiple trips of up to 6 months each. An ETA does not guarantee entry to the UK. For studies exceeding 6 months, a UK Student Visa is required instead.

MX.visaType: Visa-Free Entry
requiredDocuments: Valid ordinary passport
Immigration card (completed on arrival for air entry)
Forma Migratoria Múltiple — FMM (required for land border entry; obtain free online at inm.gob.mx before travel)

For short-term study (≤180 days): acceptance letter from a Mexican institution in the National Educational System, stating your full name, level and area of study, course name, start and end dates, fee cost, and institution contact

For short-term study: proof of economic solvency — bank statements showing an average monthly balance of approx. $2,053 CAD (or equivalent) over the past 3 months, or a scholarship/employment/pension letter
MX.notes: Citizens of visa-exempt countries may enter Mexico without a visa for tourism, transit, or short-term study for up to 180 days. For study purposes carry an acceptance letter from your Mexican educational institution and proof of financial solvency. Solvency may be shown by a parent or guardian if you are under 25, or by a scholarship letter from the institution. Cross land borders with a completed FMM form. Verify current requirements at the nearest Mexican consulate or embassy before travelling.

For short-term study: proof of economic solvency — bank statements showing an average monthly balance of approx. $2,053 CAD (or equivalent) over the past 3 months, or a scholarship/employment/pension letter

For study purposes carry an acceptance letter from your Mexican educational institution and proof of financial solvency. Solvency may be shown by a parent or guardian if you are under 25, or by a scholarship letter from the institution. Cross land borders with a completed FMM form. Verify current requirements at the nearest Mexican consulate or embassy before travelling.

GB.visaType: Student Visa (UK Visas and Immigration — Student route)

MX.visaType: Visa-Free Entry
requiredDocuments: Valid ordinary passport
Immigration card (completed on arrival for air entry)
Forma Migratoria Múltiple — FMM (required for land border entry; obtain free online at inm.gob.mx before travel)

Solvency may be shown by a parent or guardian if you are under 25, or by a scholarship letter from the institution. Cross land borders with a completed FMM form. Verify current requirements at the nearest Mexican consulate or embassy before travelling.

ES.visaType: Type D Long-Stay Study Visa (Visado Nacional de Larga Duración)
ES.duration: Required for stays >90 days (full semester). Short-stay Schengen visa for visits <90 days.
requiredDocuments: Valid passport (min. 1 year validity beyond intended stay)
Completed national visa application form
2 recent passport photographs (35×45mm, white background)
University admission letter (Carta de Admisión from URJC)
Proof of sufficient funds (Erasmus grant letter + bank statements)
Health insurance valid in Spain (min. €30,000 coverage)
Proof of accommodation in Spain (rental contract or residence letter)
Criminal background check (apostilled in your country)
Medical certificate
Visa fee payment receipt (~€80)
ES.notes: Apply at the Spanish embassy/consulate in your home country at least 8 weeks before travel. Appointments must be in person. After arriving in Spain, apply for the TIE (Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero) at the Oficina de Extranjería within 30 days of arrival.

GB.visaType: Student Visa (UK Visas and Immigration — Student route)
GB.duration: Course length + additional time. For ~5 month semester, Standard Visitor may apply.
requiredDocuments: Valid passport
Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from Bangor University
Online UK visa application at gov.uk
Biometric enrolment at UK Visa Application Centre in your country
Bank statements showing funds for full stay
Proof of English language proficiency (IELTS Academic 5.5+ or equivalent)
Tuberculosis (TB) test results (if from a listed country — check gov.uk)
Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) payment — £776/year (grants NHS access)
Visa fee: £490
GB.notes: Apply for your UK Student Visa at least 6–8 weeks before the course start date. If your semester is under 6 months, confirm with Bangor University whether a Standard Visitor Visa (£115, no CAS needed) is sufficient. Your BRP (Biometric Residence Permit) will be issued in the UK — collect it from the designated Post Office within 10 days of arrival.

ES.visaType: No Visa Required — EU/EEA Freedom of Movement

GB.visaType: UK Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA)
GB.duration: Up to 6 months per visit
GB.processingTime: Usually within 1 day (up to 3 working days)
requiredDocuments: Valid passport
Digital photo of your face
Email address
Credit or debit card (£16 fee, rising to £20 from April 2026)
GB.notes: Apply via the UK ETA app or at gov.uk/eta. Links to your passport; valid for 2 years or until your passport expires (whichever is sooner). Permits multiple trips of up to 6 months each. An ETA does not guarantee entry to the UK. For studies exceeding 6 months, a UK Student Visa is required instead.

MX.visaType: Visa-Free Entry
requiredDocuments: Valid ordinary passport
Immigration card (completed on arrival for air entry)
Forma Migratoria Múltiple — FMM (required for land border entry; obtain free online at inm.gob.mx before travel)

For short-term study (≤180 days): acceptance letter from a Mexican institution in the National Educational System, stating your full name, level and area of study, course name, start and end dates, fee cost, and institution contact

For short-term study: proof of economic solvency — bank statements showing an average monthly balance of approx. $2,053 CAD (or equivalent) over the past 3 months, or a scholarship/employment/pension letter
MX.notes: Citizens of visa-exempt countries may enter Mexico without a visa for tourism, transit, or short-term study for up to 180 days. For study purposes carry an acceptance letter from your Mexican educational institution and proof of financial solvency. Solvency may be shown by a parent or guardian if you are under 25, or by a scholarship letter from the institution. Cross land borders with a completed FMM form. Verify current requirements at the nearest Mexican consulate or embassy before travelling.

PT.notes: EU/EEA citizens do not need a visa or residence permit for Portugal. GB.visaType: Student Visa (UK Visas and Immigration — Student route)
GB.duration: Course length + additional time. For ~5 month semester, Standard Visitor may apply.

Biometric enrolment at UK Visa Application Centre in your country

MX.visaType: Visa-Free Entry
requiredDocuments: Valid ordinary passport
Immigration card (completed on arrival for air entry)
Forma Migratoria Múltiple — FMM (required for land border entry; obtain free online at inm.gob.mx before travel)

For short-term study (≤180 days): acceptance letter from a Mexican institution in the National Educational System, stating your full name, level and area of study, course name, start and end dates, fee cost, and institution contact

For short-term study: proof of economic solvency — bank statements showing an average monthly balance of approx. $2,053 CAD (or equivalent) over the past 3 months, or a scholarship/employment/pension letter
MX.notes: Citizens of visa-exempt countries may enter Mexico without a visa for tourism, transit, or short-term study for up to 180 days. For study purposes carry an acceptance letter from your Mexican educational institution and proof of financial solvency. Solvency may be shown by a parent or guardian if you are under 25, or by a scholarship letter from the institution. Cross land borders with a completed FMM form. Verify current requirements at the nearest Mexican consulate or embassy before travelling.

MX.visaType: Visa-Free Entry
requiredDocuments: Valid ordinary passport
Immigration card (completed on arrival for air entry)
Forma Migratoria Múltiple — FMM (required for land border entry; obtain free online at inm.gob.mx before travel)

For short-term study (≤180 days): acceptance letter from a Mexican institution in the National Educational System, stating your full name, level and area of study, course name, start and end dates, fee cost, and institution contact

For short-term study: proof of economic solvency — bank statements showing an average monthly balance of approx. $2,053 CAD (or equivalent) over the past 3 months, or a scholarship/employment/pension letter
MX.notes: Citizens of visa-exempt countries may enter Mexico without a visa for tourism, transit, or short-term study for up to 180 days. For study purposes carry an acceptance letter from your Mexican educational institution and proof of financial solvency. Solvency may be shown by a parent or guardian if you are under 25, or by a scholarship letter from the institution. Cross land borders with a completed FMM form. Verify current requirements at the nearest Mexican consulate or embassy before travelling.

Verify current requirements at the nearest Mexican consulate or embassy before travelling.

Email address

MX.visaType: Visa-Free Entry
requiredDocuments: Valid ordinary passport
Immigration card (completed on arrival for air entry)
Forma Migratoria Múltiple — FMM (required for land border entry; obtain free online at inm.gob.mx before travel)

For short-term study (≤180 days): acceptance letter from a Mexican institution in the National Educational System, stating your full name, level and area of study, course name, start and end dates, fee cost, and institution contact

For short-term study: proof of economic solvency — bank statements showing an average monthly balance of approx. $2,053 CAD (or equivalent) over the past 3 months, or a scholarship/employment/pension letter
MX.notes: Citizens of visa-exempt countries may enter Mexico without a visa for tourism, transit, or short-term study for up to 180 days. Verify current requirements at the nearest Mexican consulate or embassy before travelling.

requiredDocuments: Form Template 6 (Modelo 6) — download at: https://aima.gov.pt/media/pages/documents/23b161701a-1772620073/modelo-6.pdf
Copy of valid passport
Copy of valid Spanish residence permit (issued by Spain as the EU Member State that granted the permit)
Criminal record from your country of nationality (or from any country where you resided for more than 1 year before Portugal) — must be duly certified and within its validity period
Proof of admission under a European Union or multilateral mobility programme — Letter of Acceptance or Statement from the Portuguese higher education institution
Proof of health insurance valid in Portugal
Proof of fee payment by bank transfer to IBAN PT50 0781 0112 0112 0014 4001 1 (as indicated on Form 6; send together with all documents)
PT.notes: Send all documents by email to comunicacao.mobilidade.ue@aima.gov.pt. In your email, indicate your expected date of entry into Portugal and expected date of departure, and state that your educational institution confirms compliance with all necessary requirements. AIMA will issue a Declaration authorising you to remain in Portugal for up to 360 days, sent electronically to the email address you provide. ⚠️ If you do NOT hold a Spanish residence permit, you must follow the standard procedures and obtain a Portuguese Student Visa (Type D) through the Portuguese diplomatic network before travelling. Contact AIMA directly at comunicacao.mobilidade.ue@aima.gov.pt for any queries.

ES.visaType: Type D Long-Stay Study Visa (Visado Nacional de Larga Duración)
ES.duration: Required for stays >90 days (full semester). Short-stay Schengen visa for visits <90 days.
requiredDocuments: Valid passport (min. 1 year validity beyond intended stay)
Completed national visa application form
2 recent passport photographs (35×45mm, white background)
University admission letter (Carta de Admisión from URJC)
Proof of sufficient funds (Erasmus grant letter + bank statements)
Health insurance valid in Spain (min. €30,000 coverage)
Proof of accommodation in Spain (rental contract or residence letter)
Criminal background check (apostilled in your country)
Medical certificate
Visa fee payment receipt (~€80)
ES.notes: Apply at the Spanish embassy/consulate in your home country at least 8 weeks before travel. Appointments must be in person. After arriving in Spain, apply for the TIE (Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero) at the Oficina de Extranjería within 30 days of arrival.

GB.visaType: Student Visa (UK Visas and Immigration — Student route)
GB.duration: Course length + additional time. For ~5 month semester, Standard Visitor may apply.
requiredDocuments: Valid passport
Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from Bangor University
Online UK visa application at gov.uk
Biometric enrolment at UK Visa Application Centre in your country
Bank statements showing funds for full stay
Proof of English language proficiency (IELTS Academic 5.5+ or equivalent)
Tuberculosis (TB) test results (if from a listed country — check gov.uk)
Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) payment — £776/year (grants NHS access)
Visa fee: £490
GB.notes: Apply for your UK Student Visa at least 6–8 weeks before the course start date. If your semester is under 6 months, confirm with Bangor University whether a Standard Visitor Visa (£115, no CAS needed) is sufficient. Your BRP (Biometric Residence Permit) will be issued in the UK — collect it from the designated Post Office within 10 days of arrival.

MX.visaType: Visa de Visitante (Visitor Visa — no work permit)
MX.duration: Up to 180 days — sufficient for the 3-week summer school
requiredDocuments: Valid passport (6+ months validity beyond travel dates)
Completed Mexican visa application form
Recent passport photograph
Proof of enrollment/invitation letter from UATx
Bank statements proving sufficient funds (~USD 1,500 minimum)
Visa fee (~USD 36)
MX.notes: Apply at the Mexican embassy or consulate serving your home country. Processing is usually 2–4 weeks. The summer school (6–8 weeks) is well within the 180-day visa validity. Upon arrival you receive an FMM card — keep it safe and return it when you leave Mexico.

GB.visaType: UK Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA)
GB.duration: Up to 6 months per visit
GB.processingTime: Usually within 1 day (up to 3 working days)
requiredDocuments: Valid passport
Digital photo of your face
Email address
Credit or debit card (£16 fee, rising to £20 from April 2026)
GB.notes: Apply via the UK ETA app or at gov.uk/eta. Links to your passport; valid for 2 years or until your passport expires (whichever is sooner). Permits multiple trips of up to 6 months each. An ETA does not guarantee entry to the UK. For studies exceeding 6 months, a UK Student Visa is required instead.

MX.visaType: Visa-Free Entry
requiredDocuments: Valid ordinary passport
Immigration card (completed on arrival for air entry)
Forma Migratoria Múltiple — FMM (required for land border entry; obtain free online at inm.gob.mx before travel)

For short-term study (≤180 days): acceptance letter from a Mexican institution in the National Educational System, stating your full name, level and area of study, course name, start and end dates, fee cost, and institution contact

For short-term study: proof of economic solvency — bank statements showing an average monthly balance of approx. $2,053 CAD (or equivalent) over the past 3 months, or a scholarship/employment/pension letter
MX.notes: Citizens of visa-exempt countries may enter Mexico without a visa for tourism, transit, or short-term study for up to 180 days. For study purposes carry an acceptance letter from your Mexican educational institution and proof of financial solvency. Solvency may be shown by a parent or guardian if you are under 25, or by a scholarship letter from the institution. Cross land borders with a completed FMM form. Verify current requirements at the nearest Mexican consulate or embassy before travelling.

MX.visaType: Electronic Authorization — SAE Portal (Sistema de Autorización Electrónica de Visitante)
MX.duration: Up to 180 days — sufficient for the 3-week summer school
MX.processingTime: Online application — approved promptly (apply before travel)
requiredDocuments: Valid ordinary passport
Completed SAE online application (via the INM SAE portal before departure)
Proof of purpose of visit (e.g. UATx acceptance letter for study purposes)
Proof of sufficient funds for your stay
Return or onward flight ticket
MX.notes: Citizens of Russia, Turkey, and Ukraine are among the few nationalities authorised to use Mexico's online SAE portal to enter by air for tourism, transit, or short-term non-remunerated studies (up to 180 days). Apply through the official INM website before travelling. Entry by land or sea still requires a standard Mexican visitor visa.
